Subject: Question on billing for long conversations and rounding

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday — the latency and cost profile looked promising. Before we move to procurement, two quick clarifying questions about billing behavior for our primary workload: long multi-turn customer support conversations (average session ~25k tokens, peaks to ~60k tokens). Specifically: 

1) How do you bucket/round token consumption for very long requests? Do you bill per-token or per-1k token window? If there's rounding, how large is the quantum?

2) We use persistent session history across a 48-hour window for the same customer (prefix reuse across many calls). Is there any amortization/credit applied for prefix reuse or long-session amortization?

3) If we commit to a 12-month committed volume, what kinds of discounts apply to the billing quantum vs. per-token list price? We're trying to model unit economics before drafting an SOW.

I attached a small session log (example_session_log.json) showing a typical 3-conversation exchange. Can you circle back with a short written summary we can include in the procurement packet?

Best,
Kelsey Ramos

Hi Kelsey — thanks for the clear examples, and appreciate the follow-up. High-level answers below; I can walk your team through details on a quick call if that helps.

1) Bucketing & rounding
- Redwood bills on a 1k-token unit for text generation/response (we report per-token, invoice rounds to the nearest 1k unit). For short calls this is equivalent to rounding up to the next 1k.
- For very long single requests (>=16k tokens), we apply the \"long-session bucket\" which uses 5k-unit billing after amortization (so billing quantum is larger but with a discount factor — see below). This reduces per-token rounding overhead for long single payloads.

2) Prefix reuse / amortization
- We credit repeated prefixes across the same session within a 48-hour active window. Practically: identical prefix bytes are deduplicated for billing up to 70% credit on the matched tokens (not applicable to generated tokens). Prefix credit is applied at invoice time and is reflected as a line-item adjustment.
- For your persistent session pattern we can enable session amortization: we amortize the initial context load across subsequent calls within a configurable window (default 24h, extendable to 72h on request).

3) Commit discounts & packaging
- Standard committed discounts are applied to list price per token. We also offer "bucket-level" concessions for customers with heavy long-session profiles: long-session bucket rate = list_price * 0.85 after commit tier.
- Example (ballpark): 12-month commit of 200M tokens/month -> 18% list discount + long-session bucket rate (0.85x) for amortized content.

- Quick call (15m) with Kimberly on pricing packaging + procurement (she's CC'd).

Kelsey — looping in a bit of pricing detail and a short proposal so procurement can start scoping. TL;DR: we can structure a blended pricing package that better aligns unit economics for long-session workloads.

Proposal summary (draft):
- Pricing primitives:
  - Base per-token list price (per 1k token unit)
  - Long-session bucket (applies to single requests >=16k tokens or amortized session charge): billed per 5k tokens, applied at 0.85x list after discount tiers
  - Prefix reuse credit: up to 70% off matched prefix tokens, applied at invoice reconciliation

- Commitment tiers (examples):
  - 50M tokens/mo -> 8% discount off list
  - 200M tokens/mo -> 18% discount + long-session bucket concession (as above)
  - 500M+ tokens/mo -> 25% discount + custom amortization window and dedicated billing SKU

- Rounding & minimums:
  - Per-request rounding to nearest bucket as described (1k or 5k).
  - Monthly invoice minimum: none by default for hosted customers; we can include a guaranteed minimum spend if your procurement team prefers predictable invoices.

Attached is a one-page proposed pricing summary and a procurement matrix we often send to our finance teams. If these numbers look directionally right, we can prepare a redline-friendly MSA and a DocuSign packet.

Markus — if you have any operational constraints or holidays that would affect amortization window SLAs, flag here.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
